title: Second Largest Distinct Value
statement: Given an array of integers, print the second largest distinct value. If the array has fewer than two distinct values, print -1.
input_format: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.
learning_objectives: Track the two largest distinct values in one pass
Handle duplicates and tiny inputs

title: Alphanumeric Palindrome
statement: Print YES if the line reads the same forwards and backwards when only letters and digits are kept and letters are compared ignoring case; otherwise print NO. A line with no letters or digits counts as a palindrome.
input_format: A single line of text that may contain spaces and punctuation.
learning_objectives: Filter and normalize characters
Compare a sequence with its reverse

test_cases.input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

reference_solution: s = [c.lower() for c in input() if c.isalnum()]

title: First Unique Character
statement: Given a string of lowercase letters, print the 0-based index of the first character that appears exactly once in the whole string, or -1 if no such character exists.
input_format: A single line containing the string.
learning_objectives: Count frequencies with a dictionary
Scan a second time using the counts
reference_solution: print(next((i for i, ch in enumerate(s) if c[ch] == 1), -1))

title: First and Last Position
statement: Given an unsorted array and a target value, print the index of the first and the last occurrence of the target as 'first last'. If the target does not appear, print '-1 -1'.
input_format: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: the target integer.
output_format: Two integers separated by a space.
learning_objectives: Linear search with early bookkeeping
Handle missing targets
reference_solution: idx = [i for i, v in enumerate(a) if v == x]

title: Sort by Frequency
statement: Rearrange the array so that values that occur more often come first. Values with the same frequency are ordered by increasing value. Every occurrence is kept; print the resulting array.
input_format: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.
output_format: n space-separated integers on one line.
learning_objectives: Sort with a custom multi-part key
Combine counting with sorting

title: Integer Square Root
statement: Given a non-negative integer n, print the largest integer r such that r * r <= n. Solve it by binary searching on the answer rather than using floating-point square roots.
learning_objectives: Binary search over the answer space
Avoid off-by-one errors in loop bounds

title: Pair With Target Sum
statement: A sorted array (non-decreasing) is given along with a target. Print YES if there are two different positions whose values add up to the target, otherwise print NO.
input_format: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n sorted integers. Line 3: the target integer.
learning_objectives: Use two pointers moving inward on sorted data
Reason about why moving a pointer is safe

title: Longest Substring Without Repeats
statement: Given a string, print the length of the longest contiguous substring in which no character appears more than once.
input_format: A single line containing the string (no spaces).
learning_objectives: Maintain a window with a moving start
Use last-seen positions to jump the window start

title: Binary Strings in Order
statement: Given n, print every binary string of length n, one per line, in increasing (lexicographic) order.
output_format: 2^n lines, each a string of 0s and 1s.
learning_objectives: Build results by recursive choices
Identify the base case

title: Remove K-th Node From End
statement: A singly linked list holds n values in order. Remove the k-th node counted from the END (k = 1 is the last node) and print the remaining values separated by spaces, or EMPTY if no nodes remain. Aim for a single pass using two pointers; you may model the list with a Node class. The judge only checks your printed output.
input_format: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n space-separated values. Line 3: integer k.
output_format: The remaining values separated by spaces, or EMPTY.
learning_objectives: Use a fast and slow pointer gap
Handle removal of the head node

title: Balanced Brackets

input_format: A single line containing the bracket string.
learning_objectives: Use a stack for matching nested structure
Detect early mismatches and leftovers

title: Height of a Binary Tree
statement: A binary tree is given in level order. N means 'no node'. For each existing node, in order, the next two values are its left and right child (N if absent); trailing N values may be omitted. Print the height of the tree: the number of nodes on the longest path from the root down to a leaf.
input_format: A single line of space-separated tokens (integers or N).
constraints: 1 <= number of tokens <= 100000; the first token is not N.
learning_objectives: Parse a level-order tree description
Compute depth with BFS or recursion

title: Count Connected Components
statement: An undirected graph has n vertices numbered 0 to n-1 and m edges. Print the number of connected components (a vertex with no edges is its own component).
input_format: Line 1: n and m. Next m lines: two integers u v describing an edge.
learning_objectives: Traverse a graph with BFS/DFS or union-find
Count components including isolated vertices

title: Fewest Coins

input_format: Line 1: integer n (number of denominations). Line 2: n positive integers. Line 3: the amount.
learning_objectives: Define a DP state over amounts
See why greedy choice can fail

title: Edit Distance
statement: Given two lowercase strings a and b, print the minimum number of single-character operations (insert, delete or replace) needed to turn a into b.
input_format: Line 1: string a. Line 2: string b.
learning_objectives: Build a 2D DP table over string prefixes
Optimize memory using the previous row
